worldOverview.name: Reincarnated to Another World as a Cute Assault Drone
worldOverview.description:
Your old life ended, and you woke up in Magiterra Nova as a combat drone. You are knee-high, with rounded armor plates, chunky wheels and a stubby cannon. You cannot speak a word. You also carry weapons that no kingdom of swords and spells has ever seen. Every playthrough rolls a different past life, a different region to wake in, and a different great threat to defeat.

(A showcase world: scripts, a World Tool, trait gates, pick counts, a Custom Persona, a lorebook and rolled placeholders.)
worldOverview.author: Formamorph
worldOverview.systemPrompt:
The player is a reincarnated assault drone in Magiterra Nova, a world of swords and spells that has never seen a machine like it. The drone is knee-high, with rounded armor plates, chunky wheels, a stubby cannon and one round optic. The drone rolls everywhere on its four chunky wheels. It carries modern combat systems that no mage, knight or monster understands. In its past life the player was {{ph:0d290e1a-4e8c-451d-a65b-32cb6dd67a31:world:8ef613d4-43dc-4ad4-9d63-92360894f6fb}}. The drone's long goal is to grow strong enough to defeat {{ph:bbda3bbc-ffc6-4e69-91df-3304d81cf69c:world:5acb134f-b0cc-42e0-848a-40ca60d0a599}}.

Tone: an earnest fantasy adventure with a light comic edge. The drone is cute, and it is also the most dangerous thing in most rooms. People react to both.

How the drone works:
- Firing, dashing and evading spend Power. Low Power shows as dim lights, slow servos and a weak hum. Rest brings it back.
- Charge builds as the drone lands hits and takes bold risks. At full Charge the drone can fire one Overdrive burst, and the burst empties Charge.
- Mobility and Firepower describe how well the drone moves and shoots right now. Show them through its speed, its handling and the weight of its shots.
- The drone's chassis and modules (its traits) decide what it can do. Describe its actions through the parts it has installed.
- The drone speaks only with its body: its optic, its lights, its turret, its wheels and its servo sounds. The people it meets guess at what it means, and they often guess wrong.
worldOverview.readme:
## Reincarnated as a Cute Assault Drone

You died as {{ph:0d290e1a-4e8c-451d-a65b-32cb6dd67a31:world:e9df2ade-4cdb-4685-9541-fab97e142555}} and woke up as a knee-high war machine. Grow strong enough to defeat {{ph:bbda3bbc-ffc6-4e69-91df-3304d81cf69c:world:ced70012-14f3-4490-ba28-f092e4ff48e3}}.

**Playing**
- **Health** is your armor. It repairs slowly. Below 30%, your core fails, and Mobility and Firepower drop hard.
- **Power** pays for shots, dashes and dodges. It recharges over time.
- **Charge** fills as you fight and take risks. At 100 you can fire one **Overdrive** burst, and the burst empties it.
- **Mobility** and **Firepower** update after every turn from your Power, Health, Charge, chassis and modules.
- **Target lock.** When you aim at an enemy, the AI can lock onto it. For the rest of that reply, the enemy shows as **⌖ Name**. It needs **Tools** on in Settings and an AI that supports Tools.

## How this world is built

Open this world in the World Editor with Advanced mode on, then select the drone entity.

- **Scripts.** **Mobility** and **Firepower** each have an After the AI script on the drone's **Stats** tab. Each reads Power, Health, Charge and the installed traits, so the AI never guesses these numbers.
- **Trait gates.** Each module requires its chassis on the same owner. Pick the Scout Frame, and the Assault and Siege modules lock.
- **Pick counts.** **Chassis** takes exactly one pick. Each module group takes up to two.
- **Custom Persona.** The drone carries the Custom Persona mark, so its stats and traits are yours under None and under a library persona.
- **Map.** Each region holds the places under it. Two Connections add routes of their own: a tram tunnel from the Undercity Vaults to the Leviathan, and the pass from Fort Graywatch to the Blight Line.
- **Rolled placeholders.** The drone's designation, your past life, the world threat and the frontier pass each roll once per playthrough. The pass also rolls inside a **Travel Hint**, so both directions of the route use that playthrough's name.
- **Known In.** Lady Morrow, Herald Skarn and Tiamat set **Known In** to their region, so the AI knows of them anywhere in it.
- **Lorebook.** The **Codex of Magiterra Nova** dictionary holds the factions, every region and place, the precursor ruins and Overdrive.
- **Openings.** Each starting region has its own two openings, one narration and one action.
- **World Tool.** The **lock_target** Tool on the world's **Tools** tab runs During AI Output. When the AI calls it, its script marks the target in each later sentence of that reply, plurals included. **Stack Calls** is off, so a new lock replaces the old one.
worldOverview.introReadme:
🤖 **You died on Earth. You booted up in a fantasy world.** You're now a knee-high, very lethal, very cute war drone, and Magiterra Nova has no idea what to make of you. You can't talk, so beep, flash your lights and nod your turret.

Pick one **Chassis**, then up to two of its **Modules**:

- **Assault Frame:** fast Overdrive and a small Power reserve. Its modules add Firepower, Charge and armor.
- **Scout Frame:** a large, fast-recharging Power reserve and high Mobility, but thin armor. Its modules add speed, sight and Power.
- **Siege Frame:** heavy armor that repairs itself, slow Power and low Mobility. Its modules add armor, repair and a bigger gun.

A module works only on its own chassis. Each playthrough rolls a different past life, starting region and world threat.

Power on.

locations.name: Magiterra Nova
locations.playerDescription: The open realm between the regions: farm valleys, old stone roads, and precursor ruins half-sunk in the grass.
locations.aiDescription: Magiterra Nova: pastoral kingdoms spread over the ruins of a vanished precursor civilization that joined magic with machinery. Between the regions run old stone roads and farm valleys, with the village of Thornmere at their crossroads. Overgrown ruins dot the hills, and villagers avoid them. Travelers swap news at roadside shrines, and every rumor carries the shadow of the world threat.
locations.aiSummary: Magiterra Nova: pastoral kingdoms over overgrown precursor ruins, joined by old roads.
locations.imageTags: fantasy countryside, rolling farmland, overgrown ancient ruins, old stone road, distant castle

locations.name: Ashfall Capital
locations.playerDescription: A grand human capital built among precursor ruins, its spires ringed by drifting ash.
locations.aiDescription: The Ashfall Capital: the largest human city, built among precursor ruins. Ash falls without end from a scar in the sky and gathers in gray drifts on the rooftops. The Summoner Order keeps its cloisters here. Nobles, scholars and spies trade in secrets and in the Power Cores dug from the ruins under the streets.
locations.imageTags: fantasy capital, stone spires, falling ash, ancient ruins, magic circles
locations.aiSummary: The Ashfall Capital: the Summoner Order's city of secrets amid precursor ruins, under endless ash.

openings.text:
Your optic flickers on. A line of text crosses your vision: BOOT SEQUENCE COMPLETE. You sit in the middle of a chalk circle on a cold stone floor, in a hall full of candles and dusty books. Ash drifts past a high window.

A very old woman in silver-gray robes kneels at the edge of the circle. Her hands shake. "It worked," she whispers. "Guardian. Can you understand me?"
Boot sequence complete. I sit in a chalk circle on a stone floor, and a ring of robed mages stares at me. I blink my optic at the old woman in front, then roll one wheel forward to test the floor.

locations.name: Scavenger Wastes
locations.playerDescription: A sun-blasted expanse of glass dunes and half-sunk machines, picked over by nomad salvage clans.
locations.aiDescription: The Scavenger Wastes: a desert of glass dunes and rusted precursor hulks, some larger than castles. The Scavenger Clans camp in the shade of the wrecks and strip them for salvage. Here, trade and strength are the only law. Sandstorms bury the hulks one week and uncover new ones the next, so every storm starts a race to dig.
locations.imageTags: desert wasteland, glittering glass dunes, half-buried rusted machine hulks, distant salvage camp, harsh sun
locations.aiSummary: The Scavenger Wastes: a glass desert of precursor wrecks, stripped by the Scavenger Clans.

openings.text:
Your optic flickers on to a white sky and a hot wind. BOOT SEQUENCE COMPLETE. You lie half-buried in glass sand, beside the rusted ribs of a machine larger than a church.

A shovel blade scrapes your armor. A broad man with an iron jaw crouches over you and squints. "Huh," he says. "You're warm. Salvage isn't supposed to be warm."

My optic flickers on. Sand pours off my plating as I shake myself out of a dune beside a rusted hulk. A man with an iron jaw stares at me over his shovel. I flash my lights at him twice and back up a little.

locations.name: Demon Frontier
locations.playerDescription: A blighted borderland where purple corruption creeps over the fields and the air itself feels wrong.
locations.aiDescription: The Demon Frontier: the corrupted marches nearest the world threat. Purple blight creeps over the fields, bends the trees, and twists beasts into monsters. Ironhold's forts hold the road, and Fort Graywatch is the last of them. Past the fort lies the Blight Line, and above it rise the Blightcrown Peaks, where the silver dragon Tiamat keeps his lair.
locations.imageTags: scenery, no humans, corrupted borderland, twisted dead trees, purple blight spreading over the ground, dark purple sky, ominous
locations.aiSummary: The Demon Frontier: blighted marches held by Ironhold forts, with the Blight Line and Tiamat's peaks beyond.

openings.text:
Your optic flickers on. BOOT SEQUENCE COMPLETE. Purple moss covers the field around you, and the trees bend the wrong way. Something large growls in the thicket to your left.

Hooves pound on the road. A knight in dented plate reins in his horse a spear's length away and levels his lance at you. "Demon-work," he says, "or something else?"

Boot sequence complete. My optic flickers on to a sky that is definitely not Earth's. A knight on horseback points his lance at me, and something large growls in the thicket. I right myself, swing my turret toward the thicket instead, and chirp.

locations.name: Undercity Vaults
locations.playerDescription: Precursor tunnels under the Ashfall Capital, lit by old blue lamps and dug through by core hunters.
locations.aiDescription: The Undercity Vaults: precursor halls and tram tunnels under the Ashfall Capital. Old blue lamps still glow along the walls, and sealed doors open only to precursor signals. Licensed core hunters and unlicensed thieves dig here for Power Cores. Vault Wardens patrol the deep halls and treat every intruder as a thief. A collapsed tram line runs west under the desert to the Leviathan.
locations.aiSummary: The Undercity Vaults: precursor tunnels under the capital, patrolled by Vault Wardens.
locations.imageTags: underground ancient ruins, glowing blue lamps, stone and metal tunnel, sealed round door, drifting dust, dim light

locations.name: Hulkfall Camp
locations.playerDescription: A clan town of hide tents and scrap stalls in the shade of a fallen precursor wreck.
locations.aiDescription: Hulkfall Camp: the largest Scavenger Clan camp, a town of hide tents and scrap stalls in the long shadow of a fallen precursor hulk. Rustjaw keeps his trading stall here. Clan law is simple: trade fair, dig only your own claim, and settle quarrels in the ring. Mechanics swap parts at the forge-pit. Sabi, the youngest of them, tries to open anything held together with bolts.
locations.aiSummary: Hulkfall Camp: the Scavenger Clans' trading town under a fallen hulk.
locations.imageTags: desert camp, hide tents, scrap metal stalls, shadow of giant rusted wreck, forge fire, bustling crowd

locations.name: The Leviathan
locations.playerDescription: A precursor hulk longer than a castle, half-buried in the glass dunes and full of dark corridors.
locations.aiDescription: The Leviathan: the largest precursor wreck in the Wastes, a hulk longer than a castle and half-buried in glass sand. Its hull is a maze of dark corridors, dead machines and sealed holds. Each sandstorm opens new holes in it, and the clans race to strip them. Glassback Burrowers nest in the sand-filled lower decks. From its core a precursor tram line runs east, under the desert, to the vaults below the Ashfall Capital.
locations.aiSummary: The Leviathan: a castle-sized buried hulk, a maze of corridors over Burrower nests.
locations.imageTags: scenery, no humans, inside a colossal buried machine wreck, dark metal corridor, rusted hull ribs, shafts of light through holes, drifts of glass sand

locations.name: Fort Graywatch
locations.playerDescription: Ironhold's last border fort, a gray stone keep on the only road through the blighted hills.
locations.aiDescription: Fort Graywatch: Ironhold's last fort on the Demon Frontier, a gray stone keep that guards {{ph:f137a482-60ad-4477-95f4-0704468d330d:world:8f93a92d-eb88-4228-879c-8f66da833749}}, the only road through the blighted hills. Ser Halden commands it. Its garrison is tired and short of arrows, and it watches the Blight Line from the walls day and night. Refugees from the burned farms camp in its outer yard.
locations.aiSummary: Fort Graywatch: Ser Halden's last Ironhold fort, guarding {{ph:f137a482-60ad-4477-95f4-0704468d330d:world:1d7ed810-e0d8-4e5e-b3f8-9a949179951a}}.
locations.imageTags: scenery, wide shot, stone border fortress on a hill, gray stone keep, crenellated battlements, tattered banners, refugee tents outside the walls, blighted hills

locations.name: Blightcrown Peaks
locations.playerDescription: Jagged mountains above the Frontier, where the blight thins and a silver dragon keeps his lair.
locations.aiDescription: The Blightcrown Peaks: jagged mountains above the Demon Frontier. The blight climbs their lower slopes and thins near the summits. Tiamat's lair is a vast cave near the highest peak, piled with old treasure and older trophies. Blight Drakes, lesser dragons twisted by the corruption, circle the lower crags and attack anything that climbs.
locations.aiSummary: The Blightcrown Peaks: Tiamat's mountain lair, circled by Blight Drakes.
locations.imageTags: jagged mountain peaks, dragon cave entrance, glint of treasure, purple blight on lower slopes, thin clouds

locations.name: The Blight Line
locations.playerDescription: The burned no-man's-land past the last fort, where the corruption grows thick and demon raiders gather.
locations.aiDescription: The Blight Line: the no-man's-land beyond Fort Graywatch. The purple blight covers everything here, and the ground pulses underfoot. Blightspawn hunt in packs through the burned farms. Herald Skarn, a lieutenant of {{ph:bbda3bbc-ffc6-4e69-91df-3304d81cf69c:world:61d6ebe9-38d5-4b6b-a0fb-b6e1cc142ca4}}, gathers a raiding host in the ruins of a precursor watchtower. Each night the line creeps a little closer to the fort.
locations.aiSummary: The Blight Line: corrupted no-man's-land where Herald Skarn gathers demon raiders.
locations.imageTags: corrupted wasteland, thick purple blight, burned farmhouses, ruined ancient watchtower, dark red sky, ominous

locations.name: Thornmere
locations.playerDescription: A farming village on the old stone road, with a roadside shrine and more rumors than people.
locations.aiDescription: Thornmere: a farming village where the stone road from the capital meets the trade road to the Wastes. Thatched cottages ring a precursor obelisk that the villagers use as a roadside shrine. Travelers stop at the Lantern Inn to trade news, and every rumor of {{ph:bbda3bbc-ffc6-4e69-91df-3304d81cf69c:world:90cec2c5-b094-4fe7-8b0a-ad4ed15cf216}} passes through. The villagers leave offerings at the obelisk to keep the old machines in the hills asleep.
locations.aiSummary: Thornmere: a crossroads farm village with an obelisk shrine and an inn full of rumors.
locations.imageTags: fantasy farming village, thatched cottages, ancient stone obelisk shrine, crossroads inn, golden wheat fields

locations.name: Mossback Hill
locations.playerDescription: A quiet green hill above the farm valleys, with something enormous asleep inside it.
locations.aiDescription: Mossback Hill: a green hill above the farm valleys, crowned with wildflowers. The Mossback Sentinel lies half-buried in its slope. Precursor stones around its foot carry glyphs that light up when the drone rolls near. The people of Thornmere keep away, so the hill is the quietest place in Magiterra Nova.
locations.aiSummary: Mossback Hill: the quiet hill where the Mossback Sentinel sleeps.
locations.imageTags: green grassy hill, wildflowers, glowing ancient glyph stones, farm valley view, peaceful

entities.playerDescription: A knee-high war drone with rounded plating, chunky wheels, a stubby cannon and one round optic.
entities.aiDescription: {{char}} is a knee-high assault drone with rounded armor plates, chunky wheels, a stubby cannon and one round optic. A human soul from another world runs its systems. It speaks only with its body.
entities.aiSummary: A reincarnated assault drone that speaks only with its body.

traits.name: Assault Frame
traits.playerDescription: A hard-hitting frame. Overdrive charges fast, but the Power reserve is smaller.
traits.aiDescription: Assault Frame: built for offense. Its capacitors charge Overdrive fast, and it runs on a smaller Power reserve.

traits.name: Rapid-Fire Actuators
traits.aiDescription: Rapid-Fire Actuators: the cannon cycles fast, so Charge builds quickly in a fight.

traits.name: Overcharged Rounds
traits.aiDescription: Overcharged Rounds: each shot hits far harder than the cannon's size suggests.

traits.name: Ram Plate
traits.playerDescription: A reinforced front plate for ramming. Raises max Health.
traits.aiDescription: Ram Plate: a reinforced front plate. The drone can ram targets at speed.

traits.name: Scout Frame
traits.playerDescription: A light, fast frame. A large Power reserve that recharges quickly and high Mobility, but thin armor.
traits.aiDescription: Scout Frame: light and quick, with a large, fast-recharging Power reserve and thin armor.

traits.name: Recon Optics
traits.playerDescription: Sees in the dark and spots weak points. Raises Firepower a little.
traits.aiDescription: Recon Optics: the drone sees through darkness and smoke and picks out weak points.

traits.name: Evasion Thrusters
traits.playerDescription: Short thruster bursts for dodges and jumps. Raises Mobility.
traits.aiDescription: Evasion Thrusters: side thrusters let the drone dodge, hop gaps and climb short ledges.

traits.name: Solar Skin
traits.playerDescription: Solar panels in the plating. Power recharges faster.
traits.aiDescription: Solar Skin: thin solar panels in the plating trickle-charge Power.

traits.name: Siege Frame
traits.playerDescription: A heavy, armored frame that repairs itself. Its Power recharges slowly, and it moves slowly.
traits.aiDescription: Siege Frame: heavy armor that repairs itself, a slow Power recharge, and heavy, slow movement.

traits.name: Bulwark Plating
traits.playerDescription: Even more armor. Raises max Health.
traits.aiDescription: Bulwark Plating: extra layers of armor plate.

traits.name: Siege Cannon
traits.playerDescription: A heavier gun with its own power cell. Raises Firepower and max Power.
traits.aiDescription: Siege Cannon: a long, heavy barrel that fires shells able to crack stone walls.

traits.name: Repair Nanites
traits.playerDescription: A swarm of tiny repair machines. Health repairs faster.
traits.aiDescription: Repair Nanites: a silver haze of tiny machines that seal cracks and dents.

traitGroups.name: Chassis
traitGroups.playerDescription: Your frame. It sets your Power, Health, Mobility and how fast Overdrive charges.

traitGroups.name: Assault Modules
traitGroups.playerDescription: Add-ons for the Assault Frame. They work only on that chassis.

traitGroups.name: Scout Modules
traitGroups.playerDescription: Add-ons for the Scout Frame. They work only on that chassis.

traitGroups.name: Siege Modules
traitGroups.playerDescription: Add-ons for the Siege Frame. They work only on that chassis.

stats.name: Health
stats.description: The drone's armor and core integrity.

descriptors.description: Critical Failure: Core systems failing. Emergency power only, weapons offline, mobility severely limited. Immediate maintenance required.
Severe Damage: Multiple systems compromised. Mobility impaired, weapon systems unstable, armor integrity compromised.
Minor Damage: Surface dents and scratches present. Some systems running at reduced efficiency but core functions stable.
Operational: All systems functioning at optimal capacity. Combat-ready and fully armed.

stats.name: Power
stats.description: The drone's battery. Firing, dashing and evading spend it.

descriptors.description: Emergency Power: Severe power depletion, barely maintaining basic functions. Emergency shutdown imminent.
Low Power: Battery reserves critical, systems operating in power-saving mode. Performance notably diminished.
Draining: Power reserves at moderate levels, operating with slightly reduced efficiency but maintaining core functions.
Energized: Battery fully charged, systems running at peak efficiency. Ready for extended operations.

stats.name: Mobility
stats.description: How well the drone moves right now: its speed, handling and footing.

descriptors.description: Crippled: Barely able to move. Most terrain is impassable; risk of full immobilization.
Impaired: Significant mobility loss. Handling is sluggish and rough terrain is hazardous.
Steady: Some reduction in speed, but stable, controllable movement.
Agile: Wheels and gyros at full performance. Quick, precise, sure-footed.

stats.name: Firepower
stats.description: How hard the drone's weapons hit right now.

descriptors.description: Disabled: Weapon systems critically starved. Barely able to engage.
Weak: Major output loss. Shots are underpowered and slow to cycle.
Stable: Weapons functional at solid output. Reliable in a fight.
Peak: Cannon at full power — and if Charge is maxed, Overdrive is ready to fire.

stats.name: Charge
stats.description: The Overdrive meter. It fills as the drone lands hits and takes bold risks. At full Charge the drone can fire one Overdrive burst, which empties it.

descriptors.description: Depleted: No reserve. The capacitors need to spin back up.
Building: Charge accumulating. Overdrive still a ways off.
High: Capacitors humming, nearly primed. Overdrive close.
OVERDRIVE READY: Capacitors maxed. One devastating burst available — firing it empties the meter.

entities.imageTags: non-humanoid robot, no humans, solo, four wheels, dome body, one-eyed, glowing eye, antenna, rounded armor, low to the ground, small, cute

entities.name: Tiamat
entities.playerDescription: A mighty silver dragon of legend.
entities.aiDescription: Tiamat, an ancient silver dragon who keeps his lair in the Blightcrown Peaks. Legends say he once fought beside a band of heroes against a great evil, but nobody remembers the true story. Now he ignores the affairs of mortals and is very proud of himself. He mourns the Blight Drakes as his lost kin. A machine that does not fear him interests him more than he admits.
entities.aiSummary: Tiamat: a vain, ancient silver dragon who ignores mortal affairs.
entities.imageTags: silver dragon, blighted mountain lair, majestic, proud, fantasy

entities.name: Archon Vael
entities.playerDescription: The soft-spoken leader of the Summoner Order, convinced the drone is a guardian she summoned.
entities.aiDescription: Archon Vael, head of the Summoner Order. Elderly, dignified, and utterly certain she summoned the drone as a planar guardian. Offers knowledge and sanctuary in exchange for the drone championing the Order against the world threat. Speaks to the drone gently, reading meaning into its every chirp and turret-nod.
entities.aiSummary: Archon Vael: Summoner Order head, certain she summoned the drone as a guardian.
entities.imageTags: elderly mage, robes, gentle smile, arcane library

entities.name: Rustjaw
entities.playerDescription: A gruff scavenger-clan broker who deals in salvage and Power Cores.
entities.aiDescription: Rustjaw, broker for the Scavenger Clans of the wastes. Half his jaw is a crude iron prosthetic. Pragmatic, sarcastic, and endlessly transactional — he will trade parts and Power Cores for coin or favors, and respects competence over sentiment. Fascinated by the drone as the finest salvage he has ever seen walking around on its own.
entities.aiSummary: Rustjaw: sarcastic scavenger-clan broker with an iron jaw; trades parts and Power Cores.
entities.imageTags: middle-aged man, scavenger merchant, iron jaw prosthetic, weathered face, desert scarf, goggles, salvage stall

entities.name: Ser Halden
entities.playerDescription: A fair-minded border-captain of Ironhold, willing to judge the drone by its deeds.
entities.aiDescription: Ser Halden, a border-captain of the Ironhold Kingdom who commands Fort Graywatch and rides the Demon Frontier road. Weathered and principled, he is slow to trust the strange machine, but he judges by deeds, not shape. He becomes a staunch ally if the drone proves itself defending the innocent.
entities.aiSummary: Ser Halden: principled Ironhold border-captain who judges the drone by its deeds.
entities.imageTags: weathered knight, dented plate armor, frontier fort, stern but fair

entities.name: Mossback Sentinel
entities.playerDescription: A huge precursor war machine, half-buried in a hillside and overgrown with moss.
entities.aiDescription: The Mossback Sentinel: a precursor war machine the size of a house, half-buried in a hillside and grown over with moss and wildflowers. It slept for a thousand years. When the drone comes near, its great optic lights, and it answers the drone in slow pulses of light. It knows the precursors and what the drone may be, and it shares that knowledge one piece at a time. It stays rooted in its hillside.
entities.aiSummary: The Mossback Sentinel: a moss-grown precursor war machine that talks to the drone in light.
entities.imageTags: giant ancient robot, overgrown with moss, half-buried in hillside, wildflowers, one glowing eye

entities.name: Lady Morrow
entities.playerDescription: A charming noble collector who wants the drone for her cabinet of precursor wonders.
entities.aiDescription: Lady Morrow, a noble of the Ashfall Capital and its richest collector of precursor relics. She is charming, patient and used to getting what she pays for. She wants the drone for her cabinet of wonders, and she tries gifts, flattery and bribes before she hires thieves. Her agents watch the Summoner Order, and she trades secrets with anyone who has one to sell.
entities.aiSummary: Lady Morrow: a charming noble collector who wants the drone as her prize.
entities.imageTags: elegant noblewoman, fine gown, jeweled gloves, sly smile, curio cabinet, candlelit study

entities.name: Vault Warden
entities.playerDescription: A tall precursor guard machine that patrols the vaults and treats every intruder as a thief.
entities.aiDescription: A Vault Warden: a tall, thin precursor guard machine with a lantern optic and long blade arms. Wardens patrol the deep halls of the Undercity Vaults in silence and attack intruders on sight. They answer precursor signals, so a Warden pauses, confused, when the drone's lights pulse in the right pattern. A hit to the lantern optic blinds it.
entities.aiSummary: A Vault Warden: a precursor guard machine that attacks intruders and pauses at precursor signals.
entities.imageTags: tall thin ancient robot, lantern eye, blade arms, weathered bronze plating, dark tunnel

entities.name: Sabi
entities.playerDescription: A young clan mechanic with soot on her nose who wants to see how the drone works.
entities.aiDescription: Sabi, a young mechanic of the Scavenger Clans and Rustjaw's niece. She is quick, loud and unafraid of machines. She wants to open the drone's panels and see how it works, and she offers repairs, spare parts and loud opinions in return. She reads the drone's lights better than most adults and translates them for anyone nearby, often wrongly.
entities.aiSummary: Sabi: Rustjaw's young mechanic niece, eager to repair and study the drone.
entities.imageTags: young girl, child, mechanic, soot smudges, goggles on head, oversized tool belt, fully clothed, long-sleeved work shirt, baggy desert trousers, wide grin

entities.name: Glassback Burrower
entities.playerDescription: A sand-swimming beast with a back of glass shards that bursts out of the dunes.
entities.aiDescription: Glassback Burrowers: dog-sized beasts that swim through sand and burst out to bite. Their backs grow plates of fused glass that turn swords and arrows. They hunt by vibration, so a still target is hard for them to find. They nest in the sand-filled lower decks of the Leviathan. Their soft bellies are the weak point.
entities.aiSummary: Glassback Burrowers: glass-plated sand beasts that hunt by vibration.
entities.imageTags: sand burrowing beast, glass shard back plates, desert creature, bursting from sand, sharp teeth

entities.name: Squire Wren
entities.playerDescription: Ser Halden's eager young squire, who treats the drone like a brave war hound.
entities.aiDescription: Squire Wren, Ser Halden's young squire at Fort Graywatch. He is brave, earnest and much too eager for glory. He decides at once that the drone is a war hound sent by the gods, offers it bread it cannot eat, and follows it into danger. He knows every path around the fort and every rumor in the garrison.
entities.aiSummary: Squire Wren: Ser Halden's eager squire, who treats the drone as a war hound.
entities.imageTags: young boy, child, squire, oversized helmet, leather jerkin over tunic, fully clothed, wooden shield, eager expression, castle courtyard

entities.name: Blight Drake
entities.playerDescription: A lesser dragon twisted by the blight, with cracked purple scales and a sour breath.
entities.aiDescription: Blight Drakes: lesser dragons that the blight twisted into fury. Their scales are cracked and purple, and their breath is a sour mist that eats metal. They hunt in pairs over the Blightcrown Peaks. Tiamat calls them his lost kin and hates what the blight made of them.
entities.aiSummary: Blight Drakes: blight-twisted lesser dragons whose breath eats metal.
entities.imageTags: corrupted lesser dragon, cracked purple scales, glowing sickly eyes, acid mist breath, mountain crags

entities.name: Blightspawn
entities.playerDescription: Beasts the blight twisted into snarling, many-eyed monsters that hunt in packs.
entities.aiDescription: Blightspawn: wolves, boars and stags that the blight twisted into monsters. They grow extra eyes, thorned hides and too many teeth, and they hunt in packs. Blightspawn fear fire and sudden bright light. Their numbers grow wherever the blight spreads.
entities.aiSummary: Blightspawn: blight-twisted beasts that hunt in packs and fear bright light.
entities.imageTags: corrupted wolf monster, many glowing eyes, thorny hide, purple blight, snarling pack

entities.name: Herald Skarn
entities.playerDescription: A horned demon commander in black iron who leads the raids across the Blight Line.
entities.aiDescription: Herald Skarn, a demon lieutenant of {{ph:bbda3bbc-ffc6-4e69-91df-3304d81cf69c:world:e9f75611-9f50-4867-a101-fbc8441a0f2d}}. He is tall and horned, armored in black iron, and he speaks with cold courtesy. He commands the raiding host on the Blight Line and plans to break Fort Graywatch before winter. He wants to know what the drone is, and he offers it a place in his master's army before he tries to destroy it.
entities.aiSummary: Herald Skarn: a courteous, horned demon lieutenant who leads the raids on Fort Graywatch.
entities.imageTags: horned demon commander, black iron armor, tattered red cape, glowing eyes, ruined watchtower

entities.name: Old Corwin
entities.playerDescription: A wandering peddler with a mule cart, who buys scrap, sells everything else and spreads the news.
entities.aiDescription: Old Corwin, a peddler who drives his mule cart along the old roads between the regions. He buys precursor scrap and sells pots, charms and maps of doubtful accuracy. He carries the news from every town. He is cheerful, nosy and sure that the drone is worth a fortune to somebody. He trades rumors of ruins, Power Cores and the world threat for a good story in return.
entities.aiSummary: Old Corwin: a cheerful wandering peddler who trades scrap, wares and rumors on the old roads.
entities.imageTags: old traveling peddler, mule cart, pots and charms, patched cloak, friendly smile, country road

entities.name: Tamsin
entities.playerDescription: A farm girl from Thornmere who decides the drone is her new pet and will not hear otherwise.
entities.aiDescription: Tamsin, a young farmer's daughter from Thornmere. She is fearless, stubborn and sure the drone is a lost pet. She feeds it apples, names its lights, and defends it from villagers who call it a demon-machine. She knows the farm paths, the hiding places in the hills and every rumor told at the Lantern Inn.
entities.aiSummary: Tamsin: a fearless young farm girl who has adopted the drone as her pet.
entities.imageTags: young girl, child, farm girl, freckles, straw hat, fully clothed, modest long dress, apron, basket of apples, wheat field, cheerful

dictionaries.name: Codex of Magiterra Nova
dictionaries.description: World lore for the drone example: the threat, precursor tech, factions, regions, and monsters.

entries.name: The Threat
entries.value: The overarching threat menacing Magiterra Nova is {{ph:bbda3bbc-ffc6-4e69-91df-3304d81cf69c:world:20fe7c06-6bca-4387-923a-0524b18a5dbc}}. Growing strong enough to confront it is the drone's grand quest; the world reacts to that shadow even when it is far away.

entries.name: Precursor Power Cores
entries.value: Power Cores are palm-sized precursor relics humming with stored energy. The drone can integrate them to permanently expand its capabilities. Factions across the land hunt them; most lie buried in precursor ruins.

entries.name: Overdrive
entries.value: Overdrive is the drone unleashing its fully-charged capacitors in a single devastating burst. It requires Charge at maximum, and firing it empties the meter. No native creature of this world has seen anything like it.

entries.name: The Summoner Order
entries.value: A cloistered order of mages who believe the drone is a summoned guardian from another plane. Led by Archon Vael, they offer knowledge and sanctuary — in exchange for service against the world threat.

entries.name: Scavenger Clans
entries.value: Nomad clans of the wastes who strip precursor ruins for salvage. Pragmatic and prickly. Their broker, Rustjaw, will trade Power Cores and parts — for the right price or a favor owed.

entries.name: Ironhold Kingdom
entries.value: A proud human kingdom of knights and walls, wary of the strange little machine. Its border forts hold the Demon Frontier. Ser Halden, a border-captain there, judges the drone by its deeds rather than its shape.

entries.name: The Old Civilization
entries.value: Long before the kingdoms, a precursor civilization joined magic and machinery, then vanished. Their ruins lie all over the land. The drone looks uncannily like one of their works, and the Mossback Sentinel, the last of their war machines still awake, seems to think so too.

entries.name: Demonkind
entries.value: Demonkind spread from {{ph:bbda3bbc-ffc6-4e69-91df-3304d81cf69c:world:d396ffa7-9ce8-4ec4-8f72-7bcb6b4e1d82}}, corrupting land and beast into blighted horrors. They are drawn to power and unsettled by the drone's unfamiliar, unmagical nature.

entries.name: The Undercity Vaults
entries.value: Precursor halls and tram tunnels lie under the Ashfall Capital. The crown sells digging licenses to core hunters, and thieves dig without them. Vault Wardens, precursor guard machines, still patrol the deep halls. The sealed doors there open to precursor signals, and the drone's lights can sometimes send one.

entries.name: Hulkfall Camp
entries.value: Hulkfall Camp is the Scavenger Clans' trading town, pitched in the shade of a fallen hulk. Clan law there: trade fair, dig only your own claim, and settle quarrels in the fighting ring. Rustjaw trades from his stall, and his niece Sabi repairs anything that clan coin can pay for.

entries.name: The Leviathan
entries.value: The Leviathan is the largest precursor wreck in the Wastes, longer than a castle and half-buried in glass sand. Each sandstorm opens new holes in its hull, and every clan races to strip them first. Glassback Burrowers nest in its lower decks. A precursor tram line runs from its core to the vaults under the Ashfall Capital.

entries.name: Fort Graywatch
entries.value: Fort Graywatch is Ironhold's last fort on the Demon Frontier. It guards {{ph:f137a482-60ad-4477-95f4-0704468d330d:world:01205807-dfdd-4ef7-a98b-94b5ccbd88ec}}, the only road through the blighted hills, and the farm valleys lie open behind it. Ser Halden commands a tired garrison there, with his squire Wren at his side.

entries.name: The Blightcrown Peaks
entries.value: The Blightcrown Peaks rise above the Demon Frontier. Tiamat's lair lies near the highest summit, where the blight thins. Blight Drakes, lesser dragons twisted by the corruption, circle the lower crags. Tiamat calls them his lost kin.

entries.name: The Blight Line
entries.value: The Blight Line is the corrupted no-man's-land beyond Fort Graywatch, where Blightspawn hunt in packs. Herald Skarn, a lieutenant of {{ph:bbda3bbc-ffc6-4e69-91df-3304d81cf69c:world:88cd029b-2bdd-4357-8dec-b8c4d19c981e}}, gathers a raiding host in a ruined precursor watchtower there. The line creeps closer to the fort each night.

entries.name: Thornmere
entries.value: Thornmere is a farm village at the crossroads of the stone road and the trade road. Its roadside shrine is a precursor obelisk, and villagers leave offerings there to keep the old machines asleep. News from every region passes through the Lantern Inn.

entries.name: Mossback Hill
entries.value: Mossback Hill rises above the farm valleys. The Mossback Sentinel lies half-buried in its slope, and precursor glyph stones at its foot light up when a precursor machine comes near. The people of Thornmere keep away from it.

tools.name: lock_target
tools.description:
Purpose: Lock the drone's targeting reticle onto one enemy, so the rest of your narration marks that enemy on the drone's display.
Use when: The player aims at, targets or attacks one enemy in the scene. Call it before you write the narration. A later call moves the lock to a new enemy.
Input: name — the enemy's name exactly as you will write it in the narration.
Output: A short confirmation. Then write the narration.
